1299	### Checkpoints
1300	
1301	Every successful `advance` that settles a node boundary — a task is
1302	completed, or a failure is submitted (whether it retries or exhausts the
1303	attempts) — writes a checkpoint in the same transaction as the state update
1304	and event append. The checkpoint stores the complete state summary at that
1305	boundary, including completed, skipped, and failed nodes, condition results,
1306	outputs, attempts with their unfinished retry counts, and the status and
1307	current iteration of every loop (with the per-iteration records), together
1308	with the position of the last written event. Because the checkpoint matches
1309	the stored state at that position, recovery can continue without replaying or
1310	duplicating any node output.
1311	
1312	Checkpoints do not add fields to the execution state and do not append events:
1313	an execution that declares no retries, timeout, or loops keeps exactly the
1314	same state shape and event stream as before.
1315	
1316	### Complete the next ready node
1317	
1318	```http
1319	POST /executions/run-1/advance
1320	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1
1321	
1322	{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
1323	```
1324	
1325	The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
1326	updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
1327	in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
1328	automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
1329	the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
1330	the status becomes `completed`.
1331	
1332	Instead of an output, a failure can be submitted for the same ready task:
1333	
1334	```http
1335	POST /executions/run-1/advance
1336	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-2
1337	
1338	{"failure":{"reason":"gateway timeout"}}
1339	```
1340	
1341	The body must contain exactly one of `output` or `failure`, and `failure`
1342	carries exactly a `reason` string. Either body may additionally carry a
1343	`worker_id` string identifying the lease holder when the execution's work
1344	item has been claimed (see "Claim a work item"). A failed task appends a `node_failed`
1345	event recording the attempt number and reason. While the task has retries
1346	left it returns to the ready set and a `node_retried` event records the next
1347	attempt number; otherwise the task is permanently failed and the execution
1348	terminates with reason `retries_exhausted`. The same rules apply to tasks
1349	inside loop bodies, which are retried within their current iteration.
1350	
1351	Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
1352	conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `failed_nodes`, `condition_results`, `outputs`,
1353	and `attempts`. `attempts` maps each attempted task to its current `attempt`
1354	number and its `failures` count; loop body tasks track the same per iteration.
1355	Executions of workflows that declare approval points additionally expose
1356	`waiting_approval` (`null`, or the pending point's `node_id`, `approvers`, and
1357	loop context) and the `approvals` record list. Each condition evaluation
1358	appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a `node_skipped` event to
1359	the execution stream.
1360	
1361	### Cancel an execution
1362	
1363	```http
1364	POST /executions/run-1/cancel
1365	Idempotency-Key: cancel-request-1
1366	```
1367	
1368	A running execution is terminated immediately with termination reason
1369	`cancelled`. Cancelling a completed or already terminated execution returns
1370	its state unchanged, and cancelling a missing execution returns 404.
1371	
1372	Execution status is `running`, `completed`, or `terminated`. A terminated
1373	execution records exactly one `termination_reason` — `retries_exhausted`,
1374	`rejected`, `timeout`, or `cancelled` — and appends a single
1375	`execution_terminated` event; completed executions keep a `null` termination
1376	reason and their own `execution_completed` event. Advancing a terminated
1377	execution returns its state unchanged without consuming the submitted output
1378	or failure; a decision against one only succeeds as a repeat of the decision
1379	that rejected it, and otherwise conflicts.
1380	
1381	### Claim a work item
1382	
1383	```http
1384	POST /executions/run-1/claim
1385	Idempotency-Key: claim-request-1
1386	
1387	{"worker_id":"worker-7","lease_seconds":30}
1388	```
1389	
1390	Claiming is how an external worker takes ownership of a running execution
1391	before advancing its ready tasks. `worker_id` is a non-empty string and
1392	`lease_seconds` is an optional positive number of seconds (default 30). The
1393	response contains the claimed `work_item` (its `execution_id` and
1394	`workflow_id`) and a `lease` recording the `worker_id`, the `lease_seconds`
1395	duration, the `expires_at` deadline, and the `heartbeat_at` active time.
1396	Each work item is held by at most one worker at a time: claiming a work
1397	item whose lease is still active — even by the same worker — is a 409
1398	`conflict`. Claiming a completed or terminated execution returns the
1399	definite empty result `{"work_item":null,"lease":null}` and absorbs no
1400	input, and claiming a missing execution returns 404.
1401	
1402	While a work item is held, results are submitted through the usual
1403	`advance` entry by including the holder's identity:
1404	
1405	```http
1406	POST /executions/run-1/advance
1407	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-3
1408	
1409	{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"},"worker_id":"worker-7"}
1410	```
1411	
1412	Submitting results for a work item held by another worker, or after the
1413	lease has expired, is a 409 `conflict` that does not change execution
1414	state. An execution that never claimed a work item accepts `advance`
1415	exactly as before, and its state fields and event stream are identical to
1416	an execution without any claim.
1417	
1418	When a lease expires, the work item returns to the claimable set and may be
1419	claimed again by the same or another worker. The second claim continues
1420	from the materialized state: node outputs and results recorded by the
1421	earlier holder are never advanced or recorded twice, and every written
1422	output belongs to the single advance that submitted it.
1423	
1424	### Renew a lease
1425	
1426	```http
1427	POST /executions/run-1/heartbeat
1428	Idempotency-Key: heartbeat-request-1
1429	
1430	{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
1431	```
1432	
1433	Within the lease period the holder may heartbeat to extend `expires_at` by
1434	the lease duration and refresh the `heartbeat_at` active time; the response
1435	carries the updated `lease`. A heartbeat never advances nodes, writes
1436	outputs, or appends node events. A heartbeat from another worker or after
1437	the lease expired is a 409 `conflict`; a heartbeat for a missing execution
1438	or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404 `not_found`.
1439	
1440	### Release a work item
1441	
1442	```http
1443	POST /executions/run-1/release
1444	Idempotency-Key: release-request-1
1445	
1446	{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
1447	```
1448	
1449	Releasing invalidates the lease immediately and returns the work item to
1450	the claimable set, so it can be claimed again right away; progress already
1451	made and the recorded events are unchanged. Releasing with another
1452	worker's identity or after expiry is a 409 `conflict`; releasing for a
1453	missing execution or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404
1454	`not_found`.
1455	
1456	Claims, heartbeats, and releases append no events and add no fields to the
1457	execution state, so replay, checkpoints, and recovery are unaffected.
1458	Leases live in the same SQLite database as the execution state, so
1459	unexpired leases and claim ownership remain valid after the service
1460	restarts.
1461	
1462	### Recover from a checkpoint
1463	
1464	```http
1465	POST /executions/run-1/recover
1466	Idempotency-Key: recover-request-1
1467	
1468	{"from":"latest_checkpoint"}
1469	```
1470	
1471	Recovery rebuilds a running execution from its latest checkpoint and returns
1472	the rebuilt execution. It appends no events and changes no state: the rebuilt
1473	execution is exactly the materialized state, and a subsequent replay has the
1474	same conclusion as before the interruption. After recovery, further
1475	`advance` calls continue from the checkpoint, so node outputs, failure
1476	reasons, attempt numbers, and loop iteration ownership are identical to an
1477	uninterrupted run; failure records for tasks inside a loop body still carry
1478	their loop id and current iteration. Recovery works after the service has
1479	been restarted, because checkpoints live in the same SQLite database as the
1480	execution state and events.
1481	
1482	A completed execution is returned unchanged, producing no new events. A
1483	terminated execution is likewise returned unchanged and the operation
1484	absorbs no input; if a timeout or cancellation takes effect between
1485	checkpoint writes, termination takes precedence over recovery. Events and
1486	checkpoints remain queryable after cancellation or timeout, and their replay
1487	stays consistent with the materialized state.
1488	
1489	Recovering a missing execution returns 404. Recovering an execution that has
1490	no checkpoint, or whose latest checkpoint cannot be parsed, returns 409
1491	`conflict`. A missing `from` field, a wrong type, or an unknown recovery
1492	origin is a 400 `validation_error`; a non-finite number in the body is
1493	rejected the same way as every other request. Reusing an idempotency key
1494	already used by another operation (including an `advance` or `cancel` on the
1495	same execution) returns 409 `conflict`.
1496	
1497	### Replay
1498	
1499	```http
1500	POST /executions/run-1/replay
1501	```
1502	
1503	Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
1504	stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
1505	and the rebuilt execution.
1506	
1507	## Errors
1508	
1509	Errors use this shape:
1510	
1511	```json
1512	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
1513	```
1514	
1515	Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
1516	return 409. An empty `X-Tenant-Id` header value is a validation error; quota
1517	declarations and the usage, bill, and metrics queries require a tenant, and
1518	quota limits are positive integers validated by the
1519	same rules as every other body (no non-finite numbers, no unknown fields).
1520	Reusing a workflow or execution identifier, adding a workflow version whose
1521	tag already exists for that workflow, or reusing an idempotency key across
1522	different operations (within the same tenant), is a conflict. Starting an
1523	execution against a missing workflow or a missing workflow version is a
1524	missing resource (`404 not_found`). Migrating an execution to a missing
1525	version is likewise a missing resource, while migrating a completed or
1526	terminated execution is a conflict; a malformed migration body is a
1527	validation error, and a migration to the version already bound is a
1528	state-returning no-op rather than an error.
1529	Exceeding a tenant's declared workflow or execution quota is also a `409
1530	conflict`, with the word "quota" in the message so it can be distinguished
1531	from an identifier conflict; the rejected request writes nothing. Referencing
1532	a resource owned by another tenant is a missing resource (`404
1533	not_found`), indistinguishable from one that does not exist, so existence is
1534	never revealed across tenants. A `retries` value that is negative, non-integer, or greater than
1535	10, and a non-positive `timeout_seconds`, are validation errors. A malformed
1536	subscription — a missing or mistyped field, an unknown field, an empty or
1537	duplicated event list, an unknown event type, an empty or non-http(s) `url`,
1538	a non-positive timeout or attempt count, more than ten attempts, a
1539	subscription declaring both `url` and `queue` or neither, an empty queue
1540	name, or a non-positive visibility timeout — is a
1541	validation error that rejects the whole request without partial writes, and
1542	querying the delivery history or the queues of a missing execution is a
1543	missing resource. Declaring a queue name another workflow or execution of
1544	the same tenant already declared is a conflict. Pulling from or
1545	acknowledging a missing queue, and acknowledging an unknown or already
1546	acknowledged message, are missing resources; a pull body that is not an
1547	empty object, or an acknowledgement body without exactly an
1548	`idempotency_key` string, is a validation error. An approval
1549	point with an empty approver list, a duplicate or non-string approver, an
1550	approval on a non-task node, and a decision body that is malformed or carries
1551	a decision other than `approved` or `rejected` are validation errors.
1552	A map node with an unknown or missing field, a mistyped or non-positive
1553	`max_instances`, an invalid template, a `source` that is not a
1554	task dependency, or an invalid `path` is likewise a validation error that
1555	rejects the whole request, whether the map stands alone or sits inside a
1556	loop body.
1557	Deleting or modifying an expanded instance whose index is out of bounds,
1558	whose map node does not exist, whose execution is missing, or that belongs
1559	to another tenant is a missing resource; deleting an instance that is
1560	waiting on an approval or already completed, or modifying any instance that
1561	has already advanced, is a conflict; a delete body that is not empty, a
1562	modify body without exactly an `input` object, and any unknown field or
1563	non-finite number are validation errors that write nothing.
1564	Re-expanding a node that is not a dynamic `map`, a missing execution, or a
1565	cross-tenant reference is likewise a missing resource; re-expanding a node
1566	that has not expanded yet, has permanently failed, has an instance waiting
1567	on an approval, belongs to a completed execution, or sits in a loop that is
1568	not currently running is a conflict; a re-expansion body that is not an
1569	empty object is a validation error that writes nothing.
1570	A decision by an approver who is
1571	not listed for the pending point, or any decision against an execution that
1572	has no pending approval point (other than a repeat of the decision that
1573	resolved the latest one), is a conflict. Claiming a work item whose lease is
1574	still active, submitting results for a work item held by another worker or
1575	after the lease expired, and heartbeating or releasing a lease held by
1576	another worker are conflicts, while heartbeating or releasing an execution
1577	with no claimed work item is a missing resource. Recovering a missing
1578	execution is a missing resource, while recovering an execution that has no
1579	checkpoint or whose latest checkpoint is unparseable is a conflict; an
1580	invalid recover body is a validation error. An invalid schedule declaration —
1581	a non-positive or non-integer interval, a malformed or out-of-range cron
1582	expression, declaring both an interval and a cron plan, an unknown missed
1583	policy, or an unknown field — is a validation error that rejects the whole
1584	request without partial writes; pausing, resuming, or updating the schedule
1585	of a missing workflow, or pausing and resuming a workflow that has no
1586	schedule, is a missing resource, and a malformed pause or resume body is a
1587	validation error. Request bodies must not contain
1588	non-finite numbers (`NaN`, `Infinity`, or overflowing values such as `1e400`);
1589	they are rejected with 400. Finite floats keep their full precision, including negative zero
1590	(`-0.0`), and every response body ends with a single newline.
1591	
1592	## Tests
1593	
1594	```bash
1595	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
1596	```
1597	
1598
